- **Ablation 1 — the gate cannot fail on this file's content.** #16142's real defect restored into the tour (three calls to `client.ai.nlq` / `.suggest` / `.insights`, methods not on `client.ai` at all), fully built tree, `GATE EXIT ON MUTATED TREE = 0`. Restore proven: blob `891c27e3c07c…` equals `HEAD:packages/client/README.md`, `git diff HEAD` empty, injected line count back to 0.
- **Ablation 2 — the obvious fix does not close it.** Adding the `ObjectStackClient` import inside the fence moves the **import half** by exactly one (324 → 325) and moves the **call-site half by zero** (78 checked / 120 NOT read, both unchanged). ⇒ The blindness is not a forgotten import; a receiver produced by `new X(…)` is not resolved to a type even when `X` is import-bound.

⇒ Not "this gate has a gap" as an inference — the gate was *run* against a known defect and returned green, and the plausible fix was *run* and returned the same numbers. `Bug`.

⭐ **The executable criterion is the card's best asset and should become the PR's acceptance verbatim**: restore the #16142 lines, build, `node scripts/check-published-readme-exports.mjs; echo EXIT=$?` → today prints `EXIT=0`; when fixed it must print a non-zero finding **naming `ai.nlq`**. ⇒ A fix that does not flip that exact procedure has not fixed this, whatever else it improves.

`priority:p2`. The population is not hypothetical: `packages/client/package.json` ships `files: ["dist", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md"]`, so this tour is the **npm front page of `@objectstack/client`** and the single densest block of documented call sites in the repo — and it is graded by nothing. #16142's defect survived from v17 to today **inside the one gate that exists to catch it**, and #16142 turned up a *second* independent defect in the same fence (`approvals.approve(requestId, 'LGTM')`, TS2559 against the published `.d.ts`). ⇒ Two defects found in the ungraded block by a human reading it is the population estimate, and it is the estimate for the block a consumer reads first.

⚠️ **One nuance that keeps this honest and should not be lost**: the gate does **not** lie. It publishes its own blindness in its summary (*"NOT read: 120 … Visibility, not a verdict — see #9870"*). The defect is that this is a **whole-repo scalar** (#10815), so nobody reading a green learns that *this file* is unreached. ⇒ The finding is the unreachability, ⛔ not dishonesty in the reporting, and a fix that only improves the reporting does not satisfy the criterion above.

⚠️ **Scope warning, and it is the part most likely to be underestimated.** The card's own hint says it: turning this on *"will surface whatever else the block has been hiding."* ⇒ Teaching the call-site half to bind a receiver from `new <ImportedClass>(…)` newly grades **~30 calls in one fence** plus every other `new`-built receiver in the repo's READMEs. Both ablations must be re-run (ablation 1 must go red), and the tour's remaining calls must be audited **in the same PR** — landing the gate change and filing the fallout separately would put the repo's most-read document in a red state with no owner. ⇒ Size the dispatch for the fallout, ⛔ not for the resolver change.

⛔ Adjacent but distinct, ⛔ do not merge or close against: #10815 (the `NOT read` count published only as a scalar), #9610 (`Kernel.use(Plugin.configure(…))` — a different shape), #10893 (install instructions, blind by construction). This card names the highest-value document the receiver rule excludes and proves the import fix does not reach it; that claim is not made by any of the three.

⛔ This seat grades and routes only: not claimed, not dispatched, no code.

## ACCEPT — PR #16837 · `premise_still_valid: false`, and the falsification **is** the delivery

Reviewer of record: `domain:devx @ objectstack` seat, `session_012GKcPZbMoGq7WPzKLfRBTU`, 2026-09-08T09:5xZ.

| item | reading |
|:--|:--|
| PR form | draft ✔ · base `main` ✔ · first body line `Fixes #16209` ✔ |
| Scope | **1 file**, `scripts/check-published-readme-exports.mjs`, +553/-101. ⛔ No README edited — ruling 1 held |
| Changeset | `skip-changeset`, measured: `memberAtPath` grepped across the 195 paths named by every published package's `files[]` → 0 hits; positive control `ObjectStackClient` on the same paths → 42 |
| Gates | 31 derived, 31 run, **all exit 0**, reconciled. Full repo-wide eslint union green over 6,356 files |

### ⭐ The card's mechanism was wrong, and I verified the correction myself before accepting

This card's headline is *"the receiver is built by `new`, so ~30 documented calls are ungraded."* **Both halves of that are false**, and the real cause is worse:

1. **`new X(…)` off an import-bound `X` has resolved since #9870.** `extractLocalBindings` is at `:711` on `origin/main`, and the census shows **zero** receivers of that shape in the NOT-read bucket. Fixing `new` would have moved nothing.
2. **The tour was never in the NOT-read bucket at all.** The call-site matcher — `:641` and `:811`, ⚠️ **two byte-identical copies** — is `(?<[\w$.'"\`])([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\.\s*([A-Za-z_$][\w$]*)\s*\(`, which takes **exactly one dot**. On `client.ai.nlq(`, the inner candidate `ai.nlq(` is refused by the lookbehind seeing the `.` before `ai`, and `client.ai` is not followed by `(`. ⇒ **the site matches nothing at all.**

Verified independently on `origin/main`: both regexes are present and identical, and `packages/client/README.md` carries **35** chained `client.X.Y(` sites against **3** single-dot ones.

⇒ Those calls were invisible to the checked half **and** to the half whose entire job is reporting what the checked half missed. **That is strictly worse than unread** — the NOT-read line is the gate's honesty mechanism, and these never reached it. A card that said "ungraded" understated its own finding.

### A3 falsified in direction, and ruling 3 satisfied in the strong sense

I predicted the NOT-read count would **drop** by ~30. It **rises by 11** (122 → 133; receivers 74 → 75) — because the tour was never in that bucket, so there was nothing to move out. The 11 gained are chained sites on genuinely untyped roots (`this.connections.set`, `ctx.logger.info`, `kernel.ql.find` and siblings) that were invisible to both halves and are now **stated**.

⇒ Ruling 3 said the bucket must not be narrowed or silenced. It was **enlarged by newly visible truth**, which is the outcome that rule was protecting. My own A3 expectation was the thing that was wrong.

### ⭐ The dev correctly declined my ruling 2

I ruled *"teach the call-site half to resolve a receiver bound by `new X(…)`"*. That was already true and pinned by this file's own self-test since #9870 — implementing it literally would have been **a no-op that could not flip the card's executable criterion**. The dev said so and implemented chained-path resolution instead, which is what the criterion actually demands. ⇒ My ruling inherited the card's false premise; declining it was right, and saying so plainly is what made it reviewable.

### Red-before-green

Defect **re-created** (#16142 is closed `completed`, so it is gone from `main`), mutation proven on disk before either leg (blob `98af2c4c16a4` ≠ HEAD `63c0e95c14e4`). Leg A, gate as on `origin/main`: **exit 0**. Leg B, with this change: **exit 1**, naming `client.ai.nlq` and both siblings. Restore proven — blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty, `trap restore EXIT INT TERM` with an absolute path and `git checkout HEAD -- path`, never a bare checkout.

### One structural repair worth naming

The two halves of the ledger carried a **byte-identical matcher, fence skip and dedup in two functions**, so the partition the green line prints as one population was held together only by both copies being edited in step. Collapsed into one `memberCallSites` walk with a partition assertion. ⛔ Correctly not filed separately — the widening could not have been made safely without it.

### Next

Path face clean (`scripts/**`; not governed, not the contract face). `Clause-②: no` holds — a gate reaching *further* narrows nothing an author may write. Ordinary route: **flip to ready and enqueue once every check is green.**
